Hi Sarah — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our discovery so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of need
- Primary use: real-time assistant for customers on GreenStream core product (support + recommendations).
- Latency target: p50 < 300ms for short responses; graceful degradation acceptable at peak.
- Integration: streaming chat responses, tool-calling for lookups.

Sizing notes you gave
- Active users: 120k monthly active, ~4k concurrent during peak windows (internal estimate).
- Estimated request mix: 70% single-turn prompts (avg 100 input tokens, 300 output), 30% multi-turn sessions (avg 600 context tokens total per session).
- Rough token volume: 4.5M tokens/day (generative output + prompts) => ~135M tokens/month. You indicated this could vary +/-40% depending on rollout.

Budget & unit economics
- You mentioned a target ~ $30-40 per 1M tokens as a target for hosted inference to be economical for the product.

Batching & concurrency assumptions (we discussed)
- Continuous batching expected (steady stream of small requests) with bursts around business hours.
- Typical concurrency pattern: baseline ~50-80 concurrent requests, peaks ~350-450 for short windows.
- We'd like to understand how continuous batching will affect unit price and latency tradeoffs.

Next steps from Redwood
1) I’ll send a pricing estimate and the batching assumptions we use to calculate unit economics (attachments).
2) Schedule a technical sync with Vivek to validate concurrency/streaming constraints — can you share a 60-minute slot Wed/Thu next week?
3) Provide sample traffic traces or a short 48-hour export if you’re comfortable — that helps tighten our cost model.

I’ve attached a short estimate and our batching assumptions sheet. Vivek and Marissa are looped in.

Thanks — talk soon.

Quick technical assumptions to feed pricing model — please edit as needed: 

1) Request/sequence assumptions
- Avg prompt tokens: 100
- Avg generated tokens: scenario A = 250, scenario B = 350
- Multi-turn sessions: accounted for separately; assume 30% of requests have a 2-3 turn context averaging 600 tokens cached per session.

2) Batching & concurrency
- Continuous batching: for small streaming requests we assume an effective batching window of 8-12ms to aggregate micro-batches across in-flight requests.
- Baseline concurrency (steady): 50-80 -> achieves medium batching efficiency (approx 2.5x token throughput improvement vs naive single-request).
- Peak concurrency (bursts): 320-400 -> achieves high batching efficiency (approx 3.5x) during the 10-20 minute spike windows.
- Overnight reranking jobs: large batch jobs use specialized CPU/GPU packing; treated separately in cost calc.

3) Unit economics (hosted, illustrative)
- We model raw compute + infra + amortized networking at three efficiency tiers:
  * Low efficiency: $68 / 1M tokens
  * Medium efficiency: $42 / 1M tokens
  * High efficiency: $28 / 1M tokens
- These map to the batching efficiencies above and sequence length mixes. Your $30-40 target sits between medium and high depending on sequence length.

4) Dedicated (reserved)
- With a committed monthly GPU pool and more aggressive quantization/packing we can push unit cost below $20 / 1M tokens at sufficient throughput (multi-month commit).

5) Latency tradeoffs
- Continuous batching windows of 8-12ms add negligible added latency to p50; p95 sensitive to queueing under high burst if concurrency limits hit per-instance thresholds — we model headroom and can reserve burst slots to keep p95 within your 800ms target.

I’ll update the batching-assumptions.xlsx with these numbers and produce a short hosted vs dedicated quote for Marissa to finalize.

—Vivek
